issues.description: The solution adds an extra 'age' attribute to Animal and uses two-parameter constructors (String name, int age) for Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat, while the problem statement's UML and the template's Main use single-argument constructors (only name). This mismatch will confuse students about the required constructor signatures and prevents compiling/running the provided example Main as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across all artifacts. Preferably align the solution with the problem statement and template by removing the extra 'age' attribute from Animal and changing constructors of Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat to accept only a single String name (and update getters/setters accordingly). Alternatively, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main to document and use the two-argument (name, age) constructors.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template's example Main instantiate animal classes (Seal, Pig, Goat) using a single String parameter (name), implying that student-implemented constructors should accept only a name. However, the solution adds an extra 'age' attribute and implements constructors that require (String name, int age). This constructor-parameter mismatch for the same conceptual entities (the animal classes) creates a mapping and API confusion for students following the problem/template example.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor contracts consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution and provide single-argument constructors (String name) for Animal subclasses to match the problem/template example; or (B) Update the problem statement, UML, and template Main example to document and demonstrate the additional 'age' attribute and require two-argument constructors (String name, int age). Ensure all example code and instructions use the same constructor signature.
